capabilities: Write content in multi-column layouts inside notes
Drag and drop images and videos into columns
Detect remote image URLs and download them, rewriting links to local embeds
Edit column content inline with debounced write-back
Open images in a full-screen lightbox with scroll-wheel zoom
extras: README is written in Chinese. The plugin was formerly named DingTalk Columns (internal ids, code fence language 'dt-columns', and class names are kept for compatibility). Installation is manual via GitHub Releases, and the manifest is flagged as not reviewed by Obsidian staff. Much of the README is a detailed bug-fix changelog covering drag-drop, IME input, and stray code-fence issues.
motivation: The author built it for low-friction image collection via dragging rather than pasting, and describes it as an engineering trade-off to keep a stable columns experience on Obsidian/CodeMirror 6.
problem: Obsidian notes are single-column, and pasting remote images leaves external links that can break or fail behind anti-hotlink CDNs.
summary: Column layout plugin that renders multi-column sections in notes, with drag-and-drop image collection and automatic download of remote images.
